extracted.intended_audience: researchers and engineers working on personalized news recommender systems (academic and industrial)
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and evaluating user modeling and ranking components for personalized news recommendation systems, including feature choices, neural architectures, attention and graph-based representations, and ranking/training objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demographic features for user representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use demographics of users (e.g., age, gender and profession) as features in user profiles because users with different demographics usually have different preferences on news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demographics can help tailor recommendations to coarse user groups; they are listed in Table 4 as a standard additional feature. Caveat: requires availability and privacy handling; may not capture within-group heterogeneity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cluster/segment features for user representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Cluster users based on characteristics and use cluster/segment membership as part of the user profile to recommend according to users' interest in different topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clustering can reduce cold-start impact and enable group-level personalization. Requires feature engineering and validation of cluster quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tag/keyword features for user representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use tags or keywords derived from clicked news to indicate user interests and build user profiles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tags/keywords provide interpretable topical signals; often used in feature-based methods. Reliability depends on tag quality and taxonomy design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Location features for user representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use user location to identify neighborhood-related news and as a context feature in user modeling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Location helps surface locally relevant content. Must manage privacy and geo-coverage issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access pattern features for user representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Leverage users' access patterns (e.g., time of access, device) to understand click behavior and session characteristics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access pattern features can be included in Table 4 as additional context; useful for session-level models (e.g., CHAMELEON).

rubrics_metrics.name: Behaviors on other platforms for user representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate user behaviors from other platforms (social media, search engines, e-commerce) to enrich user profiles and mitigate cold-start on the news platform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multi-platform signals can improve modeling when aligned, but linking data across platforms faces privacy and alignment challenges. Only a few methods (NRHUB, WG4Rec) exploit multi-platform behaviors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-short-term user interest modeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Model user interests at both long-term and short-term horizons (e.g., long-term by frequency of reading a tag; short-term by recently clicked news) to capture evolving interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combining long- and short-term representations (concat or initialize RNN) often improves dynamics modeling (e.g., LSTUR, GNewsRec, FedRec). Be aware of complexity and cold-start tradeoffs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feature-based user modeling (manual feature engineering)
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct user profiles from collections of engineered features extracted from clicked news and other user attributes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Feature-based methods can incorporate many auxiliary features (Table 4) but require expertise for feature design and validation and may be suboptimal compared to learned representations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deep learning-based user modeling (learned representations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn user representations from historical behaviors (mainly click histories) using neural networks to avoid manual feature engineering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commonly infers interests from clicks using aggregation, RNNs, attention, CNNs, Transformers, graphs. Clicks are noisy—consider augmenting with other signals (IDs, context, multi-behavior).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recency-weighted aggregation of clicked news
rubrics_metrics.description: Aggregate clicked-news representations with recency weighting (e.g., exponential discounting) so recent clicks carry higher weight in the user embedding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used by Khattar et al.; simple and efficient. May miss long-term patterns and relations among clicks.

rubrics_metrics.name: News-level attention aggregation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use an attention network over clicked-news representations to weight and aggregate them into a user representation (global or personalized queries).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methods like NAML and KRED use news-level attention. Attention query can be global (invariant) or user-generated (personalized). Efficient at test time if user representation can be precomputed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Candidate-aware attention
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute attention weights of clicked news conditioned on the candidate news representation (candidate used as query) to dynamically build user representations tailored to a candidate item.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used by DKN, DAN, KIM, TEKGR. More accurate per-candidate modeling but requires storing all clicked-news representations and is more expensive at inference.

rubrics_metrics.name: RNN-based sequential user modeling (GRU/Bi-LSTM)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use recurrent networks to model sequential dependencies between clicked news to capture user interest dynamics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EBNR, RA-DSSM adopt RNNs; strengths: modeling dynamics; weaknesses: weaker at capturing global interest and temporal diversity preferences; may be less suitable if users prefer diversity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-attention / Transformer-based user modeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply self-attention or Transformer networks to model global context of user behaviors (NRMS and Transformer variants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good at capturing global context; often outperforms strictly sequential models on news where global context and diversity matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: CNN and 3D-CNN based user modeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Use CNNs (including 3D CNN over tensor representations) and co-attention mechanisms to learn user representations from clicked-news tensors or multi-field inputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: WE3CN, FIM, SFI. Can capture local patterns (e.g., word-level relatedness); some variants include hard selection to reduce cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hierarchical interest representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Model user interests hierarchically (subtopic-level → topic-level → overall) to capture multiple granularities of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HieRec exemplifies this. Hierarchical modeling can improve matching at different granularities but increases model complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bias-aware / debiased user modeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate presentation-bias information into attentive aggregation to learn debiased user interest representations (e.g., DebiasRec).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjusts for exposure/click biases that distort inferred interests. Requires assumptions or auxiliary signals about bias sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graph neural networks to capture high-order relations
rubrics_metrics.description: Use GNNs/GCNs on behavior graphs or user-news graphs to capture high-order interactions among behaviors and between users and news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methods like CAGE, GNewsRec, GERL, GNUD exploit high-order relations. Pros: richer context and collaborative signals. Cons: much higher computational cost and difficulty handling cold-start/unseen items.

rubrics_metrics.name: User-as-graph / heterogeneous graph pooling representations
rubrics_metrics.description: Represent each user as a personalized heterogeneous graph constructed from clicks and apply graph pooling to summarize into a user representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: User-as-Graph and HG-Pool show this approach. Captures personalized structures but may be expensive and sensitive to graph construction choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporating user ID embeddings (long-term interest)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use learned embeddings of user IDs to capture long-term user preferences and fuse with behavior-derived short-term embeddings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NPA and LSTUR use ID embeddings (concatenate or use to initialize RNN). Works well for active users but poorly for cold-start users without tuned embeddings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Context features (time, device, location, referrer) in user modeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate session and contextual features to improve inference of users' current preferences (e.g., CHAMELEON, DAINN).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Context features help session-level accuracy and transient preferences. Must consider feature availability and privacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modeling heterogeneous user behaviors and multi-view embeddings
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat different user behaviors (clicks, search queries, webpage browsing, dwell time, shares, dislikes) as separate views, learn view-specific embeddings, and aggregate via attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NRHUB, CPRS, FeedRec, WG4Rec show multi-behavior modeling. Improves robustness and captures complementary signals; increases model complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong-to-weak attention / feedback distillation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use stronger feedback signals (e.g., finish, share) to distill reliable signals from weaker feedback (e.g., clicks) via attention and distillation mechanisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FeedRec uses a strong-to-weak attention network to separate real positive/negative signals. Helpful to denoise noisy implicit feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hybrid content-based and graph-based user representations
rubrics_metrics.description: Combine content-based embeddings (from clicked news) with graph-based representations learned on user-news graphs to form unified user representations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IGNN, GERL, MVL use such hybrids to leverage both content and collaborative signals. Balances strengths but still struggles for new users with sparse interactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting informative clicks via attention (global, personalized, candidate-aware)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use attention to select which clicked news are informative: global parameter queries (invariant), user-ID generated queries (personalized), or candidate-aware queries (dynamic).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Global/personalized queries are efficient as user vectors can be precomputed; candidate-aware is more precise but requires on-the-fly computation and storage of clicked-news representations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fine-grained interest matching between candidate and clicked news
rubrics_metrics.description: Match candidate news and clicked news at fine granularity (word-level interactions, entity-word interactions, subtopic-level matching, multi-field matching) for more accurate relevance estimation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methods like FIM, KIM, HieRec, AMM and 3-D CNN matching improve accuracy but are computationally intensive at inference and may not precompute user representations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance-based ranking and two-tower architectures (efficiency vs granularity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rank candidate news by measuring relevance between user and news representations (often using two-tower architecture that precomputes features for efficiency).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two-tower is efficient (precompute user/news vectors) but may miss partial matches where a candidate matches only part of a user's interests; finer matching trades off latency for accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigating filter bubble: diversity, novelty and serendipity
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjust ranking strategies to introduce diversity, novelty or serendipity (e.g., rank by novelty relative to user's clicked news, refine by popularity/recency) to mitigate recommending only similar content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems like Newsjunkie and SCENE combine relevance with novelty/popularity/recency. Important for broadening exposure, but must balance user satisfaction and engagement metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinforcement learning / contextual bandits for long-term optimization
rubrics_metrics.description: Use contextual bandits (e.g., LinUCB) or deep RL (e.g., DQN, policy learning) to optimize long-term rewards and enable exploration that may discover new user interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LinUCB is efficient and has provable behavior in some settings; deep RL can optimize long-term engagement but may sacrifice short-term CTR. Evaluation requires careful unbiased estimation or online testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exploration vs short-term reward tradeoff
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize RL-based methods can explore to improve long-term user experience but may reduce immediate click-through rates compared to greedy relevance-based ranking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design reward functions (e.g., combine clicks and activeness) and exploration strategies carefully (e.g., Dueling Bandit Gradient Descent) to balance long/short-term goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short news lifecycles impact on design
rubrics_metrics.description: Because most news articles have very short lifecycles (days), models should learn news embeddings from content (not only ID) to handle cold/unseen news and the rapid vanishment of collaborative signals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Graph-based collaborative signals are limited in inference due to many cold news items; content encoders and fast update strategies are important in news domains.

rubrics_metrics.name: User modeling as document modeling and use of PLMs
rubrics_metrics.description: Formulate user modeling as document modeling where clicked-news texts form a user 'document' and apply pre-trained language models (PLMs) to improve representation quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PLM-based approaches (e.g., RMBERT, UNBERT variants) can transfer NLP advances to user modeling. Computational cost and input-length constraints must be handled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal diversity preference
rubrics_metrics.description: Account for users' tendency to click somewhat different items from their past clicks (preference for temporal diversity or serendipity), which makes strict sequential modeling suboptimal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sequential RNNs and causal self-attention may underperform compared to models emphasizing global context; model choice should consider diversity preference findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Noisy and sparse click behavior challenges
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge that clicks are noisy implicit signals and that user behavior on news platforms can be sparse, making it difficult to infer accurate interests from clicks alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mitigate via additional signals (context, multi-behavior, cross-platform), debiasing mechanisms, and stronger feedback modeling (dwell-time, finish, share).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cold-start handling for users and news
rubrics_metrics.description: Address cold-start problems: new users lack tuned ID embeddings; new news items lack collaborative history—models should rely more on content/context or cross-platform data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Techniques: content-derived news embeddings, multi-platform behaviors, cross-domain alignment. Privacy and data linking constraints may limit applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computational cost and inference-efficiency considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Be aware that candidate-dependent (fine-grained/candidate-aware) user representations and graph-based architectures generally increase inference cost and latency compared to precomputable two-tower models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose architectures balancing accuracy and latency constraints; consider hard selection, pruning, or approximation techniques to reduce runtime cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training objectives and data sparsity
rubrics_metrics.description: Training can be done via rating-prediction losses (MSE) when explicit ratings exist, but explicit feedback is sparse in news; implicit-feedback objectives and sampling strategies are common.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use appropriate loss functions for implicit signals (e.g., pairwise ranking, cross-entropy on clicks), and apply unbiased evaluation techniques when possible; MSE on sparse explicit ratings is often insufficient.
